newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone cannot rule out 1997 albumin charge.
newsitem.headline: Rhone cannot rule out 1997 albumin charge.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc SA finance director Jean-Pierre Tirouflet said he could not rule out further charges for a voluntary recall of albumin products in 1997.
"We believe today that it will have no impact in 1997. But I will not put my head on the block. We will analyse the situation," he told a news conference on Friday.

Rhone-Poulenc took a 81 million franc charge in the third quarter of 1996 for the recall by the Centeon joint-venture between its Rhone-Poulenc Rorer drugs unit and Germany's Hoechst and said total charges in 1996 would be between 100 and 200 million francs.
He noted that Rhone-Poulenc was not charging half the costs for Centeon.
The joint venture is not consolidated in the group results but falls under the line in the accounts for equity in net earnings of affiliated companies.

Whatever the total charge at Centeon, Rhone will take half of that amount in pre-tax at the affiliated level. It will be able to reduce that by about a third on the tax level and can further cut its net income charge by charging minorities because it does not have full control over Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.
